Subject: Onramp lane: environment bootstrapping & MAP items

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput numbers look promising for our inference use case. We want to move quickly on a short evaluation (2–3 week) MAP to validate latency at our peak payloads and sanity-check integration (API keys, org scoping, IP allowlisting, and optional VPC peering).

Can you send over a concise MAP with the specific environment setup steps and a recommended close timeline? Particularly:
- How we get API keys scoped to a test org (and rotation guidance)
- IP allowlist format you need and whether CIDR blocks are acceptable
- VPC peering prerequisites (AWS account IDs, security groups) and any expected maintenance windows
- A minimal checklist for the first 48 hours of load testing

We can share an infra contact (AWS account ID and preferred IP ranges) after we align on the sequence.

Best,
Sam
Head of Platform Engineering
Mediva Health

Sam — thanks, glad the demo was useful. Putting a tight MAP below and attaching a working spreadsheet with responsibilities (MAP-action-items-v1.xlsx). Short version here with owners and a proposed 14-day close cadence.

MAP summary (two-week rapid evaluation):
1) Org & API keys (owner: sofia_ivanova) — Day 0–1
   - We create a test org namespace for Mediva and invite your primary admin account.
   - We will generate a pair of API keys: a short-lived test key (30d) for the sandbox and a read-only key for metrics ingestion.
   - Rotation guidance: rotate test key on day 7; production rotation plan discussed post-eval.

2) IP allowlist (owner: marissa_cole) — Day 0
   - Provide CIDR list (comma-separated). We will validate against our firewall template and confirm reachability.
   - Example format we accept: 203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.12/32

3) VPC peering (owner: karthik_iyer) — Day 1–4 (optional for throughput parity testing)
   - We need your AWS account ID and the VPC ID to prepare a peering request.
   - Peering prerequisites: no overlapping CIDRs, routing table update, and security group rule to allow TCP/443 between peers.
   - We will schedule the peering during a low-impact window; typical completion: 1–2 business days.

4) Load/runbook checklist (owner: sofia_ivanova) — Day 2–7
   - Smoke test endpoint, verify token scoping, run 3 short bursts (100 concurrent streams, 4k tokens) and a sustained run (20s QPS for 30 minutes).
   - We capture latency p95/p99 and token cost.

Next steps and call suggestion:
- If you can confirm a contact for VPC/networking and share the CIDRs and AWS account ID, we’ll start org creation and keys today.
- I’ve attached a short MAP workbook; please add names to the owner column.
- Can we book a 30-minute kickoff tomorrow at 10:00am PT to pull in your infra lead?

Attachments: MAP-action-items-v1.xlsx (outline + timeline)

—
Sofia Ivanova

Hi Sam — looping in the quick network playbook and a lightweight VPC peering template (vpc-peering-template.csv). A few pragmatic notes from the ops side:

- API key scoping: we can issue project-scoped keys that only talk to the Mediva test org. For early testing we recommend traffic be routed via the hosted API (no peering) to reduce setup friction; peering gives lower egress cost and reduces variance in latency numbers.

- IP allowlist checks: provide 2–3 /32s or a /24 for your test machines. We will run an allowlist validation and return a signed confirmation once the rules are applied.

- Peering logistics: please send the AWS account ID and preferred VPC ID (example: vpc-0a1b2c3d). If you prefer we can initiate a cross-account support ticket and coordinate with your cloud team to expedite a same-day window.

- Timeline reality check: to get reliable p99s under production-like load, plan to run the sustained test on Day 5 after the peering has stabilized; otherwise expect warm-up variance.

I’ve added the network checklist to the MAP workbook and set tentative dates in column D. If you approve, we’ll start the org creation and key issuance immediately after the kickoff call.

Attachments: vpc-peering-template.csv

—
Marissa Cole
